topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causes.

topics.label: Concepts of cancer etiology, genetics, and environmental risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of cancer etiology by examining how intrinsic mutations, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures contribute to cancer development.

topics.label: Pathogens and viral mechanisms in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of infectious agents and multi-factorial viral processes in driving cancer development.

topics.label: Direct and metabolically activated chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens cause DNA damage and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate non-mutagenic factors in carcinogenesis, focusing on tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and tissue- or developmental-stage susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for detecting and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Balancing carcinogenic risk and lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing and summary, addressing the practical balance of carcinogenic risk in everyday life.
